items.quote: In Edmonton, the river passes through the centre of the city in a northeasterly direction
items.note: The article names it as the North Saskatchewan throughout; only river through the city.

items.quote: is an indoor amusement park located in the West Edmonton Mall in Edmonton, Alberta, Canada
items.note: World Waterpark article also says it is located within the West Edmonton Mall.

items.quote: After joining the NHL, the Oilers won the Stanley Cup on five occasions: 1983–84, 1984–85, 1986–87, 1987–88, and 1989–90
items.note: Reworded to ask how many; the quote states five occasions.

items.quote: Gretzky, along with enforcer Marty McSorley and centre Mike Krushelnyski, were traded to the Los Angeles Kings on August 9, 1988
items.note: Q4 no longer names the Oilers, which was the old giveaway for Q3. It still says 'Edmonton traded', which tells a room Edmonton had an NHL team, but in an Edmonton round Q3 is guessable anyway; acceptable.

items.quote: On June 1, 2021, the team formally announced that the new Edmonton team name would be the Edmonton Elks
items.note: Formerly the Edmonton Eskimos (to 2020), briefly the 'Edmonton Football Team' in between; the new name is unambiguous.

items.quote: Fort Edmonton (also named Edmonton House) was the name of a series of trading posts of the Hudson's Bay Company (HBC) from 1795 to 1914
items.note: Minor: the first Fort Edmonton shared a palisade with the North West Company's Fort Augustus, so a keen room might say 'North West Company'. Fort Edmonton itself was always the HBC post, so the answer stands.

items.quote: Fox was born on June 9, 1961, in Edmonton, Alberta
is composed of four glassed pyramids built around a central service core
items.note: 'Display' shuts out the 'fifth minor skylight pyramid' over the foyer. Small wrinkle, not enough to argue: the article says 'The two larger pyramids are 660 m2... and the two medium-sized ones are 410 m2', so 'large' could be read as two. Dropping 'large' ('How many glass display pyramids...') would remove even that; optional.

items.quote: which is used only by the High Level Bridge Streetcar, a historic streetcar route operated by the Edmonton Radial Railway Society
items.note: Same article: 'Opened as a bilevel bridge in 1913'. Seasonal (summer) operation of the streetcar is not stated in this article beyond holiday weekends in its early years; widely documented by the Radial Railway Society as a May to October service, so the wording is fine.

items.quote: Edmonton hosts several large festivals each year, contributing to its nickname, "Canada's Festival City"
items.note: Edmonton has other nicknames (City of Champions, Gateway to the North), but the festival clue pins it to this one. Accept 'Canada's Festival City'.
